title: Minigut Cellular Proteome and Secretome
projectDescription: A mouse minigut Organoid model analysed using quantitative proteomics to measure proteins expressed in the crypt and villi –like cellular states, additionally providing novel details of the secreted proteins associated with these conditions.
sampleProcessingProtocol: The cell samples were prepared using a filter assisted sample preparation (FASP) protocol.  In brief the samples were denatured using a lysis buffer of 4 % SDS, 0.1M DTT in 0.1M Tris-HCl, pH 7.6, using a combination of heat and ultrasonication. The protein lysate (60 µg) was transferred into centrifugal molecular weight filter (30 kDa MWCO, Millipore). Buffer exchange (x2) using a urea buffer (8M urea in 0.1M Tris-HCl pH 8.0) was used to displace SDS. The reduced cysteine residues were then alkylated using iodoacetamide (0.5 M, 20 min in darkness), followed by buffer exchange (x2) to remove the alkylating agent. After buffer exchange to the digestion buffer (0.1 M Tris-HCl pH 8), sequencing grade modified trypsin was added (1:30), followed by overnight incubation at 370C. The digests were then acidified and desalted using Sep-Pak C18 solid phase extraction cartridges (Waters). The digests of the cell samples were analyzed by LC-MS/MS with an Easy-nLC 1200 coupled to Q Exactive HF (Thermo Fisher Scientific).
dataProcessingProtocol: The mass spectrometry raw files were searched against a UniProt FASTA sequence database of the mouse proteome (version June 2016, 17,042 entries) using MaxQuant software version 1.5.5.1 with the Andromeda search algorithim. Trypsin digestion, with a maximum of two missed cleavages, carbamidomethylation of cysteine as a fixed modification, and variable modification of methionine oxidation and N-terminal acetylation were specified in the searches. A false discovery rate (FDR) of 0.01 at the peptide and protein level was applied. Label free quantification (MaxLFQ) was used with the match between run option enabled. The search results were further pre-processed and filtered using Perseus software. Identifications from the reversed sequence search, non-mouse contaminants and proteins only identified by variably modified peptides were removed. Protein LFQ values were log2 transformed followed by filtering to retain proteins with two valid values in at least one group (ENRI, ENRC or either media). Missing values were imputed as half the minimum intensity. Statistical analyses were made for both the imputed and un-imputed data using the Reproducibility-Optimized Test Statistic (ROTS). The latter results were cross-checked to avoid the masking of clear differences resulting from detection in one condition alone.
